title: Ombudsman Institutions — Lokpal, Lokayuktas and Administrative Accountability

content.overview: Ombudsman institutions (Lokpal at the Centre and Lokayuktas in the States) provide non-judicial mechanisms for investigating complaints of corruption and maladministration against public functionaries. They complement, but do not replace, judicial review and criminal process.
content.glance: Identify the institution (Lokpal/Lokayukta); state its statutory mandate, jurisdiction and powers; note the limits relative to courts and criminal investigation.
content.study: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 establishes the Lokpal for the Union and provides for Lokayuktas in the States. These institutions investigate allegations of corruption against specified public functionaries. Their powers are statutory and subject to the Constitution. They do not oust judicial review or the jurisdiction of criminal courts. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the 2013 Act and the relevant State Lokayukta legislation. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Institutional Design
sections.body: Lokpal (Centre) and Lokayuktas (States) are statutory ombudsman bodies for corruption and related maladministration complaints.

sections.heading: Jurisdiction and Powers
sections.body: Investigation, inquiry and recommendation powers as defined by the parent statute; subject to constitutional limits.

sections.heading: Relationship with Courts and Police
sections.body: Ombudsman process complements judicial review and criminal investigation; it does not replace them.

sections.heading: Accountability Value
sections.body: Provides an accessible complaint route for citizens against specified public functionaries.

examples.title: Complaint route
examples.body: A citizen alleges corruption by a specified public servant. The Lokpal/Lokayukta statutory process provides an investigation route parallel to, not instead of, criminal and judicial remedies.

hypotheticals.question: Does filing a Lokpal complaint bar a writ petition?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not automatically. Alternative remedy principles may affect maintainability, but constitutional judicial review is not ousted.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Lokpal prosecute on its own?
hypotheticals.analysis: Powers are defined by the parent statute; prosecution typically proceeds through the designated criminal process.

distinctions.title: Ombudsman process vs judicial review
distinctions.right: Constitutional supervisory jurisdiction and binding orders

misconceptions.correction: It complements judicial and criminal process; it does not oust them.

misconceptions.trap: Every administrative grievance is a Lokpal matter.
misconceptions.correction: Jurisdiction is limited to the categories and functionaries specified in the parent statute.

cases.name: Tata Cellular v Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts review legality of administrative action.
cases.relevance: Judicial review remains available alongside ombudsman mechanisms.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should an ombudsman problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the institution and statute. II. Test jurisdiction. III. Note relationship with courts. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Statutory mandate; jurisdiction; limits; relationship with judicial/criminal process; precise relief.

examTips: State the complementarity with judicial review.
Do not treat ombudsman as a substitute for courts.
